description: TWO instances of the SAME block on the SAME screen, with DIFFERENT handlers, on top of job:block-events-reactive. It proves three things that a single consumer does not show: (a) each IMobileBlockInstanceWidget has its own IEventHandler, with Handler pointing to distinct screen actions, and the event now has 2 IEventHandler consumers + 1 ITriggerNode; (b) the handler does NOT need the contract names - RatingPicker2_OnRate is called Score/Label and the link is made by the EXPRESSION of the argument, not by name (that only holds in the visual authoring of section 3.5); (c) the argument expression runs in a SUMMED scope: it sees the event parameters (Rating, Comment) AND the screen variables (LastComment), as 'Comment + " / " + LastComment' demonstrates. Along the way, OnRate becomes IsMandatory true and the module stays valid because BOTH instances have a handler - the opposite half is in tests/jobs/block-events-mandatory-reactive.json.

ops._why: 1. mandatory: each instance now owes a handler

ops.name: SecondScore
ops._why: 2. the second consumer stores elsewhere, so the two instances are not confused

ops.name: RatingPicker2_OnRate
ops._why: 3. DIFFERENT handler, with input names that are NOT those of the contract (Score/Label, not Rating/Comment)

ops.name: RatingPicker2
ops._why: 4. the second instance of the SAME block, with its own input and its own handler
scope of the EVENT: Rating is the contract parameter, transformed before reaching the handler
the scope SUMS: Comment comes from the event, LastComment is a SCREEN variable - both in the same expression
5. the screen shows what each instance produced, separately
instance 2: ANOTHER Handler key, and Arguments 2 as well - the two IEventHandler are distinct objects
a single contract for both instances
state after: 2 IEventHandler (one per instance) + 1 ITriggerNode; the block gained no trigger
each handler is used by ONE instance, not by both
